note: The OLG provides comprehensive coverage of FNS 850.2 time-limited participation requirements. Core rule: The 3-month/36-month time limit, 20-hour weekly work requirement, and ABAWD definition are clearly stated across multiple pages (ABAWD Work Rules Overview, Introduction to the SNAP Work Rules). Screening: The OLG explicitly requires workers to screen every client aged 18-64 for ABAWD exemptions at application and recertification using the SNAP Work Rules Screening page in BEACON (ABAWD Work Rules Exemptions: 'You must screen every client who is aged 18 through and including age 64'; ABAWD Work Rules Overview: 'Step 1: Screen for Exemptions'; Introduction to SNAP Work Rules: 'BEACON will automatically direct you to this page when the client is required to be screened'). Screening questions reset at every reapplication and recertification. Verification: The OLG covers verification of participation at recertification (ABAWD Work Rules Participation: 'Non-exempt clients who previously verified participation must verify it again at recertification'). Participation tracking: BEACON's ABAWD Clock page tracks strike history and participation months, with monthly batch processing to check compliance. Exception months: Covered in ABAWD Work Rules Regaining Process — must be consecutive, can only be used once per clock period. Good cause: Dedicated OLG page (Good Cause Criteria for Not Complying with the ABAWD Work Rules) covers valid reasons for non-compliance including crisis situations, temporary health problems, transportation issues, and domestic violence. The OLG also covers the disqualification process, strike issuance, and regaining eligibility. While the FNS text frames these requirements through QC verification procedures (reviewer must verify status, examine agency records, explore eligibility during field investigation), the underlying policy requirements — screening, tracking, exceptions, exemptions, good cause — are all thoroughly addressed in the OLG with BEACON procedures.
